vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: d8063c30dd05ca71e7b2d8d78360af6835dd5e46 replaced per-entry fs.RootPath calls in pkg/archive/tar.go with cachedRootPath.get. A previously validated parent path can therefore be reused after an earlier archive entry mutates that parent into a symlink, allowing later extraction or hardlink resolution to follow stale state outside the unpack root. CVE-2025-47290 is currently PUBLISHED and GHSA-cm76-qm8v-3j95 is not withdrawn.

atomic_bic.evidence: git log --all -S cachedRootPath -- pkg/archive/tar.go shows only the add in d8063c30dd05ca71e7b2d8d78360af6835dd5e46 and its two later reverts. The BIC is a single-parent commit that directly adds the cache and routes applyNaive and hardlinkRootPath through it.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: Immediate parent 2fda52edee18f9eaf573521b6620d2f5b6473781 contains no cachedRootPath and still resolves archive parents with live fs.RootPath calls, so the vulnerable cache behavior is absent.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: The BIC is not a squash or merge. Merge b1924f1fd27b66cc6528f36a53c9ea7585b3d707 has d8063c30dd05ca71e7b2d8d78360af6835dd5e46 as its second parent, and the first-parent-to-second-parent member range contains only that BIC.

affected_release_membership.evidence: The BIC is an ancestor of v2.1.0-beta.0 and v2.1.0 but not v2.0.11; cachedRootPath is present in the two v2.1.0 tags and absent in v2.0.11. This matches the vendor statement that 2.1.0 is affected.

fixed_release_membership.evidence: Release-branch fix ac00b8e6108c6925ef4ab39e9b87e956a2efdabf is not in v2.1.0 and is an ancestor of v2.1.1; cachedRootPath is absent from v2.1.1. The v2.1.1 release note identifies CVE-2025-47290 as introduced in 2.1.0.

direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched_state.evidence: 38c9bb93a38f1cef7453aa9fd28f16e00bde557d directly reverts the BIC; advisory-referenced merge cada13298fba85493badb6fecb6ccf80e49673cc has that revert as its second parent. The release/2.1 cherry-pick ac00b8e6108c6925ef4ab39e9b87e956a2efdabf has the same stable patch-id, and the direct fix patch-id equals the reverse BIC patch-id.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The BIC commit object names human author and committer Adrien Delorme and a human Co-Authored-By trailer for Corentin REGAL. Its message has no Generated-with, Copilot, Cursor, Claude, GPT, bot identity, or other AI marker; attribution was judged from this BIC only.

findings: The primary record identifies the correct vulnerability mechanism, atomic BIC, immediate parent, release boundaries, and direct fixes.
The NOT_AI verdict is supported because the vulnerable lines first appear in the human-authored BIC and that commit object has no AI marker.
